findings.title: Uses Queue shutdown APIs unavailable on supported Python versions
findings.body: `queue.Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were introduced in Python 3.13. On earlier supported runtimes, `shutdown()` raises `AttributeError` (which is only logged here), leaving idle worker threads permanently blocked in `get()`. Moreover, if a worker handles any exception, evaluating `except queue.ShutDown` at line 142 also raises `AttributeError`, terminating that worker. Use a version-compatible sentinel/condition-based shutdown mechanism, or explicitly require Python 3.13 everywhere this consumer can run.

findings.title: Queue pool has no backpressure and can grow without bound
findings.body: Each work queue is created with the default unbounded `queue.Queue()`, so `submit()` at line 212 never blocks when a worker or a particular queue is slow. The Kafka consumer can therefore continue accepting messages indefinitely while work accumulates in memory, eventually causing an OOM rather than applying the documented “natural backpressure when queues fill up.” Configure a bounded queue size and ensure the processing strategy/poll loop handles a full queue safely.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown abandons queued work instead of draining it
findings.body: `shutdown()` sets every worker's `shutdown` flag before requesting queue shutdown. A worker that finishes its current item exits on the next loop condition even when its queue still contains items, so queued offsets remain outstanding and work is not processed. `join()` then invokes this shutdown path as well, despite its expected role of waiting for in-flight work. This causes processed-but-uncommitted or partially processed results to be replayed after a normal consumer shutdown, risking duplicate side effects; drain queues before stopping workers and perform a final commit of completed offsets.

findings.title: Processing failures are acknowledged and committed
findings.body: The worker catches every exception from `result_processor` but unconditionally calls `complete_offset` in `finally`. The commit loop will then advance the Kafka offset past a failed result, permanently dropping it instead of retrying or routing it through the consumer's failure handling. This also contradicts the strategy's stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing. Only mark an offset complete after success, or explicitly route failures to an appropriate retry/DLQ path.
